access_continuity_justification: The organization has three owners, fametrano, giacomocaironi and pmazzocchi, each an admin of every repository and a reviewer of the publishing environments. If one becomes unavailable, the other two can still close issues, merge changes and release. https://github.com/btclib-org/.github/blob/main/GOVERNANCE.md#continuity
accessibility_best_practices_justificati: btclib is a library with no user interface, so accessibility practices have no surface to apply to. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib/blob/main/README.md
assurance_case_justification: ASSURANCE_CASE.md states the threat model, the trust boundaries, the secure-design argument and the argument against common implementation weaknesses this criterion asks for. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib/blob/main/ASSURANCE_CASE.md
automated_integration_testing_justificat: test.yml runs the suite on every pull request that changes more than the prose files it names. integration-bitcoind.yml runs tests/integration against Bitcoin Core on regtest on every pull request and push to main. Both are required checks. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib/blob/main/.github/workflows/test.yml
build_non_recursive_justification: This tree builds no native binaries, so there is no recursive-build question to answer. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib/blob/main/pyproject.toml
build_preserve_debug_justification: No native build or installation step exists to strip or preserve debugging information. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib/blob/main/pyproject.toml
build_repeatable_justification: Every week sdist-rebuild.yml rebuilds the latest release's sdist from its tag. It passes only if the rebuilt file matches the release's attested digest byte for byte. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib/blob/main/.github/workflows/sdist-rebuild.yml
build_reproducible_justification: The sdist is built with SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH from the commit. sdist-rebuild.yml rebuilds a release from its signed tag and verifies it against the release's PyPI attestation, and RELEASING.md tells a user how to do the same. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib/blob/main/.github/workflows/sdist-rebuild.yml
build_standard_variables_justification: btclib is pure Python built with uv_build, so no compiler or linker runs for CC, CFLAGS or LDFLAGS to reach. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib/blob/main/pyproject.toml
bus_factor_justification: fametrano wrote almost all of the code and is the only person who knows it in depth. The claude account in the contributors graph comes from the Co-Authored-By trailer on AI-assisted commits, almost all of them fametrano's. pmazzocchi, an organization owner, did the 2026-09-30 security review and has contributed some changes. In the last year, outside contributors have made only small changes. giacomocaironi, also an organization owner, wrote early parts of the code but has made no commit since 2023. The organization owners administer every repository. Knowledge of the code rests on fametrano alone. https://github.com/btclib-org/.github/blob/main/GOVERNANCE.md#continuity https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib/graphs/contributors
code_of_conduct_justification: btclib-org/.github's CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md is this repository's code of conduct, through GitHub's organization-wide default; the community-profile API reports it. https://github.com/btclib-org/.github/blob/main/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md
code_review_standards_justification: REVIEWING.md states what a review checks, how a finding is written and what clears a pull request; the part shared by every repository is followed by what this tree checks in particular. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib/blob/main/REVIEWING.md
coding_standards_enforced_justification: ruff-check, ruff-format and mypy run in .pre-commit-config.yaml, which the required lint check runs on every pull request. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib/blob/main/.pre-commit-config.yaml
coding_standards_justification: pyproject.toml's [tool.ruff] selects every rule (select = ["ALL"]) with a documented ignore list, and [tool.mypy] runs in strict mode. CONTRIBUTING.md names both and the commands that run them. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib/blob/main/pyproject.toml
contribution_requirements_justification: CONTRIBUTING.md states the coding-standard, lint-gate and 100%-coverage requirements a contribution must meet before it can land. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md
contributors_unassociated_justification: The significant contributors are fametrano and pmazzocchi. pmazzocchi and fametrano are associated: both are CheckSig co-founders, as their GitHub profiles state. In the last year, outside contributors have made only small changes. giacomocaironi, also an organization owner, wrote early parts of the code but has made no commit since 2023. https://github.com/fametrano https://github.com/pmazzocchi
copyright_per_file_justification: Every Python file opens with "Copyright (c) The btclib developers", e.g. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib/blob/main/src/btclib/__init__.py
crypto_algorithm_agility_justification: btclib implements the Bitcoin protocol, whose consensus rules fix secp256k1, SHA-256 and the signature schemes; another algorithm needs a soft fork first, and the project follows one when it activates. The curve and hash agility is in ecc, which btclib depends on. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib/blob/main/README.md
crypto_call_justification: btclib calls libraries for its ciphers and general hashes: curve arithmetic and signature schemes from ecc, BIP324's ChaCha20 and ChaCha20-Poly1305 from cryptography, hashes from hashlib. It writes what Bitcoin's specifications build on them (MuHash3072, the BIP324 key schedule) and these primitives: SipHash-2-4, which BIP152, BIP158 and the headers presync need, a private ChaCha20 block function inside MuHash3072 that encrypts nothing, and Bitcoin Core's Python copy of RIPEMD-160, used only where hashlib has none. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib/tree/main/src/btclib
crypto_certificate_verification_justific: btclib performs no network communications and so uses no TLS. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib/blob/main/docs/source/guide.rst
crypto_credential_agility_justification: btclib has no configuration file or credential store: a private key or password is a function argument, never read from or written to a file. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib/blob/main/SECURITY.md
crypto_keylength_justification: The keys btclib works with are secp256k1 keys, about 128 bits of security, above NIST's 112-bit floor for 2030; BIP324's ciphers use 256-bit keys. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib/blob/main/SECURITY.md
crypto_password_storage_justification: btclib authenticates no user and stores no password. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib/tree/main/src/btclib
crypto_pfs_justification: btclib.p2p.bip324 implements BIP324's key schedule: the session keys come from an ElligatorSwift ECDH over the key pair BIP324 makes fresh for each connection, and both ciphers rekey every 224 packets. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib/blob/main/src/btclib/p2p/bip324.py
crypto_published_justification: btclib imports its curve arithmetic from ecc, which calls btclib-secp256k1 (bindings to Bitcoin Core's libsecp256k1) wherever a call can use them and otherwise runs Python arithmetic; SECURITY.md states when each applies and `ecc.curves.is_libsecp256k1_serving()` tells a caller which. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib/blob/main/SECURITY.md
crypto_random_justification: btclib draws randomness only from Python's `secrets` module (the BMS nonce, the transaction input and output shuffle, the headers presync's commitment offset and salt); ECDSA nonces are deterministic (RFC 6979). Key, mnemonic and nonce generation is in ecc and btclib-wallet, which hold their own entries. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib/tree/main/src/btclib
crypto_tls12_justification: btclib performs no network communications and so uses no TLS. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib/blob/main/docs/source/guide.rst
crypto_used_network_justification: btclib does not communicate over a network, as docs/source/guide.rst states. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib/blob/main/docs/source/guide.rst
crypto_verification_private_justificatio: btclib performs no network communications and so uses no TLS. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib/blob/main/docs/source/guide.rst
crypto_weaknesses_justification: btclib's only SHA-1 is Bitcoin script's OP_SHA1, which the protocol requires and which runs with usedforsecurity=False. The curve schemes and ECIES are ecc's. SECURITY.md documents where a secret reaches the Python fallback. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib/blob/main/SECURITY.md
dco_justification: main requires the lint / Sign-off check, which refuses a pull request with a commit that lacks its author's Signed-off-by: trailer. Dependabot's, pre-commit.ci's and claude[bot]'s commits are exempt. https://github.com/btclib-org/.github/blob/main/.github/scripts/check_sign_off.py
delivery_unsigned_justification: Releases are published to PyPI and GitHub Releases and installed with pip from PyPI, all over HTTPS. No package or hash is fetched over plain HTTP. https://pypi.org/project/btclib/ https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib/releases
dependency_monitoring_justification: Dependabot version updates are configured in .github/dependabot.yml, and Dependabot security updates are enabled on the repository. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib/blob/main/.github/dependabot.yml
description_good_justification: btclib is a type annotated Python library for teaching, learning and using bitcoin, focused on elliptic curve cryptography and bitcoin's blockchain. https://btclib.org/btclib/
discussion_justification: GitHub supports discussions on issues and pull requests.
documentation_achievements_justification: README.md shows the OpenSSF Best Practices badge, linked to this project's page. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib/blob/main/README.md
documentation_architecture_justification: ARCHITECTURE.md documents the module layout and layer boundaries of this tree's software. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib/blob/main/ARCHITECTURE.md
documentation_basics_justification: README.md says what btclib does, how to install it and where constant time ends, and the documentation holds the API reference. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib#readme https://btclib.readthedocs.io/
documentation_current_justification: docs.yml builds the docs with -W -n on every pull request, and the build is a required check. The API reference is generated from the shipped docstrings. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib/blob/main/.github/workflows/docs.yml
documentation_quick_start_justification: docs/source/guide.rst is a task-oriented quick start, and tests/docs_examples_test.py runs its examples, so a stale example fails the suite. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib/blob/main/docs/source/guide.rst
documentation_roadmap_justification: ROADMAP.md, organization-wide in btclib-org/.github, is reviewed every September and states what is maintained, what is intended and what is deliberately not. This repository's README.md and CONTRIBUTING.md link it. https://github.com/btclib-org/.github/blob/main/ROADMAP.md
documentation_security_justification: SECURITY.md's *Limitations, not vulnerabilities* states what a user can and cannot expect: constant-time behaviour, key zeroization, and which operations use libsecp256k1 and which the Python fallback. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib/blob/main/SECURITY.md
dynamic_analysis_enable_assertions_justi: The suite runs under pytest, which rewrites `assert` statements, and the fuzz and mutation jobs run the library with assertions enabled (no `-O`). https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib/blob/main/.github/workflows/test.yml
dynamic_analysis_fixed_justification: No fuzzing or mutation-testing finding is an exploitable vulnerability, and the weekly fuzz and mutation runs on main pass. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib/actions/workflows/fuzz.yml https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib/actions/workflows/mutation.yml
dynamic_analysis_justification: Every release runs the test suite before it is published. release.yml calls test.yml, and the PyPI upload runs only if it passes. The suite fails below 100% coverage, branches included. ClusterFuzzLite fuzzing and cosmic-ray mutation testing also run every week. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib/blob/main/.github/workflows/release.yml https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib/blob/main/.github/workflows/fuzz.yml
dynamic_analysis_unsafe_justification: This tree ships pure Python, a memory-safe language; it produces no software written in a memory-unsafe language for a dynamic memory-safety tool to run against. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib/blob/main/pyproject.toml
external_dependencies_justification: The library's and its tooling's Python dependencies are declared in machine-readable form in pyproject.toml's [project.dependencies] and dependency-groups, resolved and pinned in the committed uv.lock. The btcd comparison in the fuzz tooling declares its Go modules in fuzz/btcd_decode/go.mod and go.sum, and .clusterfuzzlite/Dockerfile names its base image. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib/blob/main/pyproject.toml
floss_license_justification: The MIT license is approved by the Open Source Initiative (OSI).
floss_license_osi_justification: The MIT license is approved by the Open Source Initiative (OSI).
governance_justification: The organization's GOVERNANCE.md documents how decisions are made and every role. This tree's README.md and CONTRIBUTING.md link it. https://github.com/btclib-org/.github/blob/main/GOVERNANCE.md
hardened_site_justification: https://btclib.org/btclib/ sends Content-Security-Policy (with frame-ancestors 'none'), X-Frame-Options: DENY, X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff and Strict-Transport-Security. Check with curl -sI https://btclib.org/btclib/ The repository on github.com sends all four. PyPI's project page https://pypi.org/project/btclib/ sends all but the CSP; that is PyPI's to set. The documentation site https://btclib.readthedocs.io/ is served by Read the Docs over HTTPS with Strict-Transport-Security and X-Content-Type-Options nosniff, and no Content-Security-Policy or X-Frame-Options; that is Read the Docs' to set. Measured with curl -sIL on 2026-11-12.
hardening_justification: ruff's select = ["ALL"] includes the bandit S rules, so unsafe deserialization, weak temp files and shell injection fail the lint gate. CodeQL also runs on every pull request, every push to main and weekly. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib/blob/main/.github/workflows/codeql.yml
implement_secure_design_justification: ASSURANCE_CASE.md's *Secure design principles* argues how each principle applies to ARCHITECTURE.md's layers. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib/blob/main/ASSURANCE_CASE.md
input_validation_justification: Every public function validates its inputs and refuses what is invalid; the unchecked work lives in a private twin the public function calls once it has validated, as CONTRIBUTING.md requires. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md
installation_common_justification: btclib is on PyPI, so pip install and pip uninstall install and remove it. README.md gives the command. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib/blob/main/README.md
installation_development_quick_justifica: uv sync installs the whole development environment in one command. CONTRIBUTING.md's *The environment and the gates* gives it. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md
installation_standard_variables_justific: Installation is pip install, which follows pip's own install-location conventions; the project has no installer of its own. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib/blob/main/pyproject.toml
interact_justification: The home page says how to install btclib and links the documentation, the issue tracker, CONTRIBUTING.md, the security policy and private vulnerability reporting. https://btclib.org/btclib/
interfaces_current_justification: ruff's UP and FA rules flag deprecated standard-library and typing constructs. pytest runs with filterwarnings = ["error"], so a deprecation warning fails the suite, and deps-latest.yml runs it weekly against each dependency's newest release. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib/blob/main/pyproject.toml
internationalization_justification: btclib produces no end-user text to localize; its output is hex, addresses and error messages for developers. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib/blob/main/README.md
know_common_errors_justification: ASSURANCE_CASE.md argues how each common implementation weakness (CWE-20, 209, 248, 330/338, 347, 502, 755, 843 and others) is countered in this tree. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib/blob/main/ASSURANCE_CASE.md
know_secure_design_justification: The primary developer wrote the assurance case, which argues each secure-design principle against the architecture. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib/blob/main/ASSURANCE_CASE.md
license_location_justification: Non-trivial license location file in repository: <https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib/blob/main/LICENSE>.
license_per_file_justification: Every Python file states "Distributed under the MIT software license, see the accompanying LICENSE file or https://opensource.org/license/mit", e.g. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib/blob/main/src/btclib/__init__.py
maintenance_or_update_justification: Only the latest release is supported (SECURITY.md). For upgrading, RELEASING.md runs griffe check against the previous tag, and RELEASE_NOTES.md lists each breaking change with its before and after. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib/blob/main/RELEASE_NOTES.md
no_leaked_credentials_justification: detect-secrets runs in pre-commit against .secrets.baseline, and GitHub secret scanning with push protection is on. No secret-scanning alert is open. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib/blob/main/.secrets.baseline
osps_ac_01_01_justification: The btclib-org organization requires two-factor authentication of every member and allows only secure second factors (TOTP, security keys/passkeys, GitHub Mobile; no SMS), so no account can read or change a repository's sensitive settings without MFA. https://github.com/btclib-org/.github/issues/1362#issuecomment-5903994882
osps_ac_02_01_justification: A new member gets read access, the organization's base permission (gh api orgs/btclib-org --jq .default_repository_permission). Every higher grant is assigned by hand, through an issue in btclib-org/.github that an owner other than the one asking approves. https://github.com/btclib-org/.github/blob/main/GOVERNANCE.md#how-a-decision-is-made
osps_ac_03_01_justification: The main-self-merge ruleset requires a pull request for every change to main. Its one bypass actor, fametrano, holds it in pull_request mode, which excuses the approval but still refuses a direct push, so nobody pushes to main directly. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib/blob/main/REPOSITORY.md
osps_ac_03_02_justification: The main-integrity ruleset forbids deleting main and has no bypass actor. https://github.com/btclib-org/.github/blob/main/README.md#branch-protection-and-rulesets
osps_ac_04_01_justification: The default GITHUB_TOKEN is read-only at the organization and the repository, and cannot approve pull requests. Every workflow also sets permissions: contents: read at the top. https://github.com/btclib-org/.github/blob/main/README.md#tokens-publishing-scanning
osps_ac_04_02_justification: Every workflow sets permissions: contents: read at the top, and a job adds a write scope only where it uses it. zizmor's excessive-permissions audit runs in the required lint check. https://github.com/btclib-org/.github/blob/main/README.md#what-every-workflow-does
osps_br_01_01_justification: No workflow uses pull_request_target or workflow_run. Event fields and inputs reach run: steps only through env:, and zizmor's template-injection audit in the required lint check refuses the unsafe form. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib/blob/main/.pre-commit-config.yaml
osps_br_01_03_justification: Pull-request runs use the pull_request and pull_request_review_comment triggers, which give a fork no secrets and a read-only token. The review job, which holds a secret, runs only when the head repository is this one. On issue_comment, the mention job, which holds a secret on any pull request, checks out the default branch. https://github.com/btclib-org/.github/blob/main/.github/workflows/reusable-claude-review.yml
osps_br_01_04_justification: mutation.yml's profile is a choice from a fixed list. verified-signatures.yml's before and after are read by the called workflow through env: and refused unless they are commit shas. kernel-differential.yml's seed is free text: it reaches the shell only through env: and is passed to pytest as one quoted argument, so it cannot inject a command, and nothing else checks its value. A release tag's name is checked against the package version before anything is built. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib/blob/main/.github/workflows/kernel-differential.yml https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib/blob/main/.github/workflows/mutation.yml
osps_br_02_01_justification: Each release has a unique calendar version, YYYY.M.D, set by a signed v* tag. release.yml refuses a tag that differs from the package version or is not on main, and PyPI never accepts a version twice. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib/releases
osps_br_02_02_justification: Every release asset carries the version in its file name: the sdist, the wheel, the CycloneDX SBOM and the attestation bundle. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib/releases/latest
osps_br_03_01_justification: Every official channel the project lists is served over HTTPS only: the GitHub repository, its issue tracker and advisories, and the documentation at https://btclib.readthedocs.io/.
osps_br_03_02_justification: Releases are distributed through PyPI and GitHub Releases, both HTTPS only. PyPI files carry PEP 740 attestations and the GitHub release a Sigstore bundle. https://pypi.org/project/btclib/
osps_br_04_01_justification: Every release from v2026.8.7 on has a RELEASE_NOTES.md entry, listing what a user must act on, breaking and security changes included, and its GitHub release body is that entry. Each also has a changelog entry listing every change: CHANGELOG.md holds the latest release and changelog/ the earlier ones. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib/blob/main/RELEASE_NOTES.md https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md
osps_br_05_01_justification: Python dependencies come from PyPI, and the required test check runs the suite with uv from the committed uv.lock with --locked. pre-commit installs its hooks at the revisions .pre-commit-config.yaml names. Third-party actions are pinned by commit SHA. https://github.com/btclib-org/.github/blob/main/README.md#uvlock
osps_br_06_01_justification: Every PyPI file from 2026.8.7 on carries a PEP 740 attestation from Trusted Publishing. Every GitHub release from v2026.8.21 on carries a Sigstore provenance bundle covering each asset's SHA-256. Release tags are signed from v2026.8.21 on. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib/releases/latest
osps_br_07_01_justification: Secret scanning and push protection are on, so a push carrying a recognised credential is refused. The detect-private-key and detect-secrets hooks run in the required lint check. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib/blob/main/.secrets.baseline
osps_br_07_02_justification: A secret is an environment secret that only the owners reach. A secret kept in any other store is recorded in the REPOSITORY.md of the repository that uses it, and btclib-org/.github's tests/secrets_test.py refuses an unrecorded one. A secret is rotated when an owner changes or an exposure is suspected. The secrets kept outside an environment are rotated before they are a year old, and the list is reviewed yearly. https://github.com/btclib-org/.github/blob/main/README.md#tokens-publishing-scanning
osps_do_01_01_justification: The user guide, docs/source/guide.rst, and the API reference are published at https://btclib.readthedocs.io/. tests/docs_examples_test.py runs the guide's examples.
osps_do_02_01_justification: CONTRIBUTING.md says where a defect is filed, and the bug-report form asks for what a report needs. SECURITY.md sends a vulnerability to a private channel instead. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib/blob/main/.github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/bug_report.yml
osps_do_03_01_justification: SECURITY.md gives the gh attestation verify command for the release assets, and RELEASING.md the check that rebuilds the sdist from its tag. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib/blob/main/SECURITY.md
osps_do_03_02_justification: The verify command pins the signer and the source: --owner btclib-org and --signer-workflow the workflow that signed, and it compares the certificate's sourceRepositoryIdentifier with this repository's id, which a rename keeps, so an attestation from any other repository or workflow is refused. SECURITY.md names the signer of each release. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib/blob/main/SECURITY.md
osps_do_04_01_justification: SECURITY.md's *Supported versions*: only the latest release is supported, and nothing is backported. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib/blob/main/SECURITY.md
osps_do_05_01_justification: SECURITY.md's *Supported versions*: only the latest release is supported, so a release stops receiving security updates when the next one is published. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib/blob/main/SECURITY.md
osps_do_06_01_justification: pyproject.toml states why each runtime dependency is there. Dependencies come from PyPI through uv, are pinned in uv.lock, and are updated by weekly grouped Dependabot pull requests with a seven-day cooldown. https://github.com/btclib-org/.github/blob/main/README.md#dependabot-and-pre-commitci
osps_do_07_01_justification: CONTRIBUTING.md's *The environment and the gates* gives the build: uv is the only prerequisite, uv sync builds the environment from uv.lock, and uv build makes the sdist and wheel. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md
osps_gv_01_01_justification: btclib-org/.github's GOVERNANCE.md, *Roles*, names who holds access to sensitive resources. fametrano is the maintainer. Every owner, named there by login, is an administrator of every repository and a reviewer of the publishing environments. https://github.com/btclib-org/.github/blob/main/GOVERNANCE.md#roles
osps_gv_01_02_justification: btclib-org/.github's GOVERNANCE.md, *Roles*, describes the maintainer, the owners, repository collaborators, contributors, reviewers, the review bot, Dependabot and pre-commit.ci, and what each owes. https://github.com/btclib-org/.github/blob/main/GOVERNANCE.md#roles
osps_gv_02_01_justification: Proposed changes and usage questions are discussed publicly in the repository's issues, which have a question form, and pull requests. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib/issues
osps_gv_03_01_justification: CONTRIBUTING.md explains the contribution process: an issue first, one subject per pull request, the local gates, the review and the landing. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md
osps_gv_03_02_justification: CONTRIBUTING.md states what a contribution must meet: one subject, a Signed-off-by trailer on every commit, the gates CI runs, 100% line and branch coverage, and a review against REVIEWING.md. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md
osps_gv_04_01_justification: A grant of write or admin, to any repository of the organization, is an issue in btclib-org/.github that states the reason, and an owner other than the one asking approves it there. https://github.com/btclib-org/.github/blob/main/GOVERNANCE.md#how-a-decision-is-made
osps_le_01_01_justification: main requires the lint / Sign-off check, which refuses a commit that lacks its author's Signed-off-by: trailer, Dependabot's, pre-commit.ci's and claude[bot]'s aside. Web commits are signed off automatically. https://github.com/btclib-org/.github/blob/main/.github/scripts/check_sign_off.py
osps_le_02_01_justification: The source code is under the MIT license, which the OSI approves. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib/blob/main/LICENSE
osps_le_02_02_justification: The released wheels and sdist declare License-Expression: MIT, the same OSI-approved license as the source. https://pypi.org/project/btclib/
osps_le_03_01_justification: The license text is the repository's root LICENSE file. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib/blob/main/LICENSE
osps_le_03_02_justification: The LICENSE file ships in every release asset: at the sdist root and in the wheel's .dist-info/licenses/. https://pypi.org/project/btclib/#files
osps_qa_01_01_justification: The repository is public on GitHub at a static URL. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib
osps_qa_01_02_justification: Git history on GitHub records every change with its author, committer, date and signature. main refuses force-pushes and requires linear history. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib/commits/main
osps_qa_02_01_justification: pyproject.toml declares the direct dependencies ([project] dependencies, optional extras and dependency groups), and the committed uv.lock resolves and pins them. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib/blob/main/pyproject.toml
osps_qa_02_02_justification: The release is pure Python. Every GitHub release from v2026.8.21 on attaches a CycloneDX SBOM, generated from the built wheel and covered by the release attestation. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib/releases/latest
osps_qa_03_01_justification: main requires the CI status checks that REPOSITORY.md's Required checks on main names. enforce_admins is off, so an admin merge without them is a manual bypass, which the control allows. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib/blob/main/REPOSITORY.md#required-checks-on-main https://github.com/btclib-org/.github/blob/main/README.md#branch-protection-and-rulesets
osps_qa_04_01_justification: The organization standard's *Which repositories, and how far* lists every btclib-org repository and its tier. https://github.com/btclib-org/.github/blob/main/README.md#which-repositories-and-how-far
osps_qa_04_02_justification: Each release is built from this repository alone. The sibling packages it depends on are released from their own repositories. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib
osps_qa_05_01_justification: No generated executable is committed. The binary files are Bitcoin-serialized data (blocks, transactions, scripts, P2P messages) used as test data and fuzz seeds, and the Sphinx inventories python.inv and ecc.inv. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib
osps_qa_05_02_justification: The binary files are Bitcoin-serialized data (blocks, transactions, scripts, P2P messages) used as test data and fuzz seeds, which the library itself decodes, and the Sphinx inventories python.inv and ecc.inv. tests/_data/README.md pins each vendored test file to its source, and docs/source/conf.py gives the command that fetches each inventory. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib/blob/main/tests/_data/README.md
osps_qa_06_01_justification: integration-bitcoind.yml runs its test suite on every pull request, and its check is required on main. test.yml runs the main suite on every pull request that changes more than the prose files it names, and its aggregate check, 'test: every job passed', is required on main. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib/blob/main/.github/workflows/test.yml
osps_qa_06_02_justification: CONTRIBUTING.md's *The environment and the gates* gives the command that runs the tests and says which workflows run them and which gate a merge. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md
osps_qa_06_03_justification: The policy is 100% line and branch coverage (CONTRIBUTING.md; standard section 8). pyproject.toml sets fail_under = 100, so untested new code fails the required test check. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib/blob/main/pyproject.toml
osps_qa_07_01_justification: The main-self-merge ruleset requires one approving review from somebody other than the author before a merge to main, and dismisses an approval on a new push. Its bypass list holds one actor, fametrano, in pull_request mode, at rest: the organization-wide bypass the maintainer kept on 2026-11-04 (btclib-org/.github#2021 and btclib-org/.github#2040). Read with gh api repos/btclib-org/btclib/rulesets/20735808 --jq '{name, bypass: [.bypass_actors[] | {actor_id, bypass_mode}], reviews: (.rules[] | select(.type == "pull_request") | .parameters | {required_approving_review_count, dismiss_stale_reviews_on_push})}', with admin rights, on 2026-11-12; actor 3296421 is fametrano (gh api users/fametrano --jq .id). GOVERNANCE.md has the maintainer add that bypass back only in an emergency, and records that it stands until the backlog settles. It is used for ordinary work: over the last two releases, 32 of the 42 pull requests merged had no approval from anybody other than their author (v2026.11.13 10 of 13, v2026.11.12 22 of 29), and fametrano merged all 32. Counted with gh pr list -R btclib-org/btclib -s merged -L 500 -S 'merged:2026-11-12T05:29:14Z..2026-11-13T00:11:34Z' --json author,reviews -q 'map(.author.login as $a | any(.reviews[]; .state == "APPROVED" and .author.login != $a) | not) | "\(map(select(.)) | length) of \(length)"' for v2026.11.13, and the same command with merged:2026-11-10T22:10:34Z..2026-11-12T05:29:13Z for v2026.11.12; who merged them, with the same search over merged:2026-11-10T22:10:34Z..2026-11-13T00:11:34Z and --json author,reviews,mergedBy -q '[.[] | .author.login as $a | select(any(.reviews[]; .state == "APPROVED" and .author.login != $a) | not) | .mergedBy.login] | group_by(.) | map("\(.[0]) \(length)")', which prints ["fametrano 32"]. https://github.com/btclib-org/.github/blob/main/GOVERNANCE.md#how-a-decision-is-made
osps_sa_01_01_justification: ARCHITECTURE.md documents the components, their layers and where the software reaches outside the process. ASSURANCE_CASE.md's *Trust boundaries* and *Threat model* name the actors and what each can do. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib/blob/main/ARCHITECTURE.md
osps_sa_02_01_justification: The API reference at https://btclib.readthedocs.io/ is generated from the docstrings of every public module, and a docs test fails when a shipped module is missing from it. CONTRIBUTING.md's *The public surface* states what is public.
osps_sa_03_01_justification: ASSURANCE_CASE.md is the security assessment: claims, threat model, trust boundaries and how each common weakness is countered. SECURITY.md's *Limitations, not vulnerabilities* records the known residual risks. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib/blob/main/ASSURANCE_CASE.md
osps_sa_03_02_justification: ASSURANCE_CASE.md's *Threat model* names the assets, the adversaries and what is not defended. Its *Trust boundaries* maps where untrusted input enters. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib/blob/main/ASSURANCE_CASE.md
osps_vm_01_01_justification: SECURITY.md's *Reporting a vulnerability* gives the private channels, a GitHub security advisory or email, and the timeframes: a report is acknowledged within 7 days, and a fix or a published advisory follows within 90 days. A report triaged as easy to rediscover is fixed as soon as possible, and its advisory is published with the fix. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib/blob/main/SECURITY.md#reporting-a-vulnerability
osps_vm_02_01_justification: SECURITY.md names the security contacts: a private GitHub security advisory, or email to security at btclib dot org. btclib-org/.github's GOVERNANCE.md, *Roles*, says that address reaches every organization owner. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib/blob/main/SECURITY.md#reporting-a-vulnerability https://github.com/btclib-org/.github/blob/main/GOVERNANCE.md#roles
osps_vm_03_01_justification: Private vulnerability reporting is enabled, and SECURITY.md points to it (the Security tab's 'Report a vulnerability') and gives an email address as the alternative. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib/security/advisories/new
osps_vm_04_01_justification: Vulnerabilities are published as GitHub security advisories on this repository, as SECURITY.md commits to. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib/security/advisories
osps_vm_04_02_justification: The CycloneDX SBOM a release attaches lists, in its vulnerabilities array, every vulnerability that the tree's .github/vex.toml judges not to affect the release, with the reason. A tree with no such judgement has no vex.toml, and its SBOM has no vulnerabilities key. https://github.com/btclib-org/.github/blob/main/README.md#12-releasing
osps_vm_05_01_justification: The standard sets the threshold: actions/dependency-review-action fails a pull request that adds or changes a runtime dependency with an advisory of moderate severity or above, or with a licence outside the allow-list. Its settings are one file, btclib-org/.github's .github/dependency-review.yml. Development dependencies are covered by the audit in the required lint check. https://github.com/btclib-org/.github/blob/main/.github/dependency-review.yml https://github.com/btclib-org/.github/blob/main/README.md#tokens-publishing-scanning
osps_vm_05_02_justification: release.yml runs uv audit over every dependency the wheel declares, and every publish job needs it to succeed. An advisory, or a service it cannot reach, stops the release. The only exemption is an id that the tree's own .github/vex.toml, carried into the release's signed SBOM, states as not affecting it. https://github.com/btclib-org/.github/blob/main/README.md#12-releasing
osps_vm_05_03_justification: The required lint check audits the whole uv.lock, every dependency group, on every pull request: check_audit.py --all-groups runs uv audit, which reads OSV's malicious-package (MAL-) entries as well as advisories. Any such entry fails the check, and so does an OSV that cannot be reached. The audit's only exemption is a .github/vex.toml entry, reviewed like any other change. The required Dependency review check also blocks a change that adds a runtime dependency with an advisory of moderate severity or above, or a licence outside the allow-list. https://github.com/btclib-org/.github/blob/main/README.md#12-releasing https://github.com/btclib-org/.github/blob/main/README.md#tokens-publishing-scanning
osps_vm_06_01_justification: The standard's section 5 sets a threshold of zero for ruff: select = ALL, bandit's S rules included, and each finding is fixed or suppressed in place with a reason. zizmor holds workflows to the same, in the required lint check. CodeQL runs on every pull request, but the standard sets no threshold for its alerts. https://github.com/btclib-org/.github/blob/main/README.md#5-ruff
osps_vm_06_02_justification: The required lint check runs .pre-commit-config.yaml on every pull request (ruff with the S rules, strict mypy, zizmor, detect-secrets) and blocks the merge on any finding not suppressed in place with a reason. CodeQL also runs on every pull request but is not a required check. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib/blob/main/.github/workflows/lint.yml
regression_tests_added50_justification: Of the pull requests merged from 2026-05-12 to v2026.11.12 that close an issue and change the library's code, under src/ or, before the code moved there on 2026-08-25, btclib/, 336 of 387 also change tests/. Counted with for w in 2026-05-12..2026-08-24 2026-08-25..2026-09-30 2026-10-01..2026-11-12T05:29:13Z; do gh pr list -R btclib-org/btclib -s merged -L 1000 -S "merged:$w" --json closingIssuesReferences,files -q '[.[] | select((.closingIssuesReferences | length) > 0 and any(.files[]; .path | startswith("src/") or startswith("btclib/")))] | [length, (map(select(any(.files[]; .path | startswith("tests/")))) | length)]'; done, which prints [118,97], [175,146] and [94,93]. The window is split because gh's search returns at most 1000 results. gh lists at most 100 files of a pull request, and of the counted pull requests it cuts short, PR 1333 also changes tests/, so the count is one short. A closed issue may be a feature as well as a bug, and a change to tests/ stands in for an added regression test. A wider proxy counts every code change, not only bug fixes: of the commits on main from 2026-05-01 to v2026.11.12 that change code under src/, which holds it from 2026-08-25, 291 of 322 also change tests/. Counted in a clone with its tags, with git log --since=2026-05-01 --format=%H v2026.11.12 -- src/ | while read c; do git show --name-only --format= $c | grep -q ^tests/ && echo tests || echo none; done | sort | uniq -c, which prints 291 tests and 31 none. Nearly all the other 31 leave behaviour as it was: a docstring, a comment, a move or a removal. The 100% line and branch coverage gate also fails a fix whose new code no test runs. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md#the-environment-and-the-gates
release_notes_justification: Non-trivial release notes file in repository: <https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib/blob/main/RELEASE_NOTES.md>.
release_notes_vulns_justification: The release notes name each advisory a release fixes by its GHSA id: v2026.10.28 to v2026.11.12 fix none and name none; v2026.10.8 names GHSA-c6h8-5hv5-3gv7. GHSA-47wq-xh8q-pfxj names 2026.9.29, which removed the function; that release's notes tell users the module moved to btclib-wallet. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib/releases/tag/v2026.11.12
repo_distributed_justification: Repository on GitHub, which uses git. git is distributed.
repo_interim_justification: development is on the main branch of https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib
repo_public_justification: Repository on GitHub, which provides public git repositories with URLs.
repo_track_justification: Repository on GitHub, which uses git. git can track the changes, who made them, and when they were made.
report_process_justification: Bugs are reported in GitHub Issues, through the bug-report form. CONTRIBUTING.md's The issue tracker says where. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib/issues
report_tracker_justification: Issues are tracked in this repository's GitHub Issues, with issue forms; cross-repository issues go to btclib-org/.github's tracker. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib/issues
require_2FA_justification: The btclib-org organization requires two-factor authentication of every member. https://github.com/btclib-org
roles_responsibilities_justification: btclib-org/.github's GOVERNANCE.md, *Roles*, describes the maintainer, the owners, repository collaborators, contributors, reviewers, the review bot, Dependabot and pre-commit.ci, and what each owes. https://github.com/btclib-org/.github/blob/main/GOVERNANCE.md#roles
secure_2FA_justification: The btclib-org GitHub organization requires two-factor authentication of every member and has 'Only allow secure two-factor methods' selected, which refuses SMS as a second factor: only TOTP apps, security keys/passkeys and GitHub Mobile are accepted. Read from the organization's security settings on 2026-09-30 and recorded at https://github.com/btclib-org/.github/issues/1362#issuecomment-5903994882
security_review_justification: pmazzocchi, an owner other than the maintainer, did a security review on 2026-09-30: https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib/issues/2450 . It is pinned to a commit, checks every claim and trust boundary of ASSURANCE_CASE.md, states what it did not cover, and files each finding as an issue.
signed_releases_justification: Every PyPI file from 2026.8.7 on carries a PEP 740 attestation, and every GitHub release from v2026.8.21 on a Sigstore provenance bundle. Release tags are signed from v2026.8.21 on. SECURITY.md gives the verify command. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib/releases/latest
sites_password_security_justification: The project sites (GitHub, PyPI, Read the Docs, btclib.org) store no passwords of this project's; authentication is theirs. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib/blob/main/SECURITY.md
small_tasks_justification: Small tasks for newcomers carry the label "good first issue", which CONTRIBUTING.md sets aside for a first contribution. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md#the-issue-tracker https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib/issues?q=label%3A%22good+first+issue%22
static_analysis_common_vulnerabilities_j: CodeQL runs on every pull request, every push to main and weekly, and ruff's select = ["ALL"] includes the bandit S rules. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib/blob/main/.github/workflows/codeql.yml
static_analysis_fixed_justification: No CodeQL alert is open, and ruff and mypy findings fail the required lint check. The earlier actions/unpinned-tag alerts, on workflows that called btclib-org/.github's reusable workflows at main, were dismissed as won't fix, and those calls are now pinned to a tagged commit. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib/blob/main/.github/workflows/claude-review.yml
static_analysis_often_justification: lint.yml (ruff, mypy) and codeql.yml run on every pull request and every push to main, and CodeQL also runs weekly. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib/actions/workflows/lint.yml https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib/actions/workflows/codeql.yml
test_branch_coverage80_justification: Branch coverage is measured (`branch = true` under `[tool.coverage.run]`) and the 100% gate includes it. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib/blob/main/pyproject.toml
test_continuous_integration_justificatio: test.yml runs the suite on every pull request that changes more than the prose files it names, and on every push to main that changes more than top-level Markdown files. Its aggregate job, test: every job passed, is a required check on main. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib/blob/main/.github/workflows/test.yml
test_justification: test.yml runs the pytest suite, gated at 100% line and branch coverage, on every pull request that changes more than the prose files test.yml names. It checks vectors from the BIPs, Bitcoin Core and Core's qa-assets, and tests/_data/README.md pins each vendored file to its upstream commit. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib/actions/workflows/test.yml
test_policy_justification: CONTRIBUTING.md makes 100% coverage a gate every change must pass, so new functionality comes with its tests. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md#the-environment-and-the-gates
test_policy_mandated_justification: CONTRIBUTING.md requires 100% coverage, and fail_under = 100.0 fails the required check for any new code without a test. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md
test_statement_coverage80_justification: pyproject.toml sets fail_under = 100.0 under [tool.coverage.report], gated on every pull request that changes more than the prose files test.yml names. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib/blob/main/pyproject.toml
test_statement_coverage90_justification: Coverage is gated at 100% (`fail_under = 100.0` under `[tool.coverage.report]`) on every pull request that changes more than the prose files test.yml names. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib/blob/main/pyproject.toml
tests_are_added_justification: The required check test: every job passed fails any pull request that leaves a line or branch untested. The merged pull requests show recent changes landing with their tests. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib/pulls?q=is%3Apr+is%3Amerged
tests_documented_added_justification: CONTRIBUTING.md documents the 100% coverage requirement, so new functionality needs a test. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md
two_person_review_justification: Over the last two releases, v2026.11.10 and v2026.11.12, 7 of 82 pull requests were approved by somebody other than the author, 9%, below the 50% the criterion asks (v2026.11.12 7 of 29, v2026.11.10 0 of 53); none was approved by somebody other than fametrano. Counted by merge time between release publications, over the same two-release window on every btclib-org project, with gh pr list -R btclib-org/btclib -s merged -L 500 -S 'merged:2026-11-10T22:10:34Z..2026-11-12T05:29:13Z' --json author,reviews -q '(map(.author.login as $a | any(.reviews[]; .state == "APPROVED" and .author.login != $a)) | "\(map(select(.)) | length) of \(length) approved, ") + "approvers \([.[].reviews[] | select(.state == "APPROVED") | .author.login] | unique)"' for v2026.11.12, and the same command with merged:2026-11-07T00:21:09Z..2026-11-10T22:10:33Z for v2026.11.10. It prints the approved count, the total and the approvers. main's ruleset requires one approving review from somebody other than the author, and fametrano holds a pull_request-mode bypass of it. https://github.com/btclib-org/.github/issues/2021
updateable_reused_components_justificati: Reused components are standard-library modules or PyPI packages pinned in uv.lock. Dependabot updates them weekly through pull requests that run the full suite. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib/blob/main/.github/dependabot.yml
version_semver_justification: Versions are calendar versions, YYYY.M.D, and each release is tagged v<version>. https://github.com/btclib-org/.github#12-releasing
version_tags_signed_justification: Release tags are signed from v2026.8.21 on, and GitHub verifies each. RELEASING.md signs each tag with git tag -s and reads the signature back after the push. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib/tags
vulnerabilities_critical_fixed_justifica: No published advisory is left unfixed. GHSA-9fr5-46w5-5f9r, rated high, was fixed in v2026.10.4, released the day it was published. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib/security/advisories
vulnerabilities_fixed_60_days_justificat: Every published advisory names the release that fixes it, and no Dependabot alert is open. GHSA-47wq-xh8q-pfxj names 2026.9.29, which removed the function; btclib-wallet 2026.10.16 fixes it. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib/security/advisories
vulnerability_report_credit_justificatio: An advisory credits its reporter as finder: pmazzocchi on GHSA-9fr5-46w5-5f9r. fametrano, the maintainer, filed the others, so they have no outside reporter to credit. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib/security/advisories
vulnerability_report_response_justificat: GHSA-9fr5-46w5-5f9r, reported privately by pmazzocchi on 2026-09-30, was fixed in v2026.10.4 and published on 2026-10-03. GHSA-9r97-9x22-2pp4 and GHSA-rw95-w37r-537w, found by fametrano, were each published with its fix the day it was opened. GHSA-47wq-xh8q-pfxj, found by fametrano, was published on 2026-10-16. btclib has no fix for it: 2026.9.29 had already removed the function, and the advisory points to btclib-wallet 2026.10.16. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib/security/advisories
vulnerability_response_process_justifica: SECURITY.md's *Reporting a vulnerability* gives the private channels (a GitHub security advisory, or security at btclib dot org), who sees a report, and how to request a CVE. Private vulnerability reporting is enabled. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib/blob/main/SECURITY.md
warnings_fixed_justification: Warnings are not tolerated: ruff, strict mypy and pytest's filterwarnings = ["error"] fail the required checks. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib/blob/main/pyproject.toml
warnings_justification: ruff runs with select = ["ALL"], mypy with strict = true and pytest with filterwarnings = ["error"], each in a required check. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib/blob/main/pyproject.toml
warnings_strict_justification: ruff runs with select = ["ALL"] and mypy with strict = true, both with zero findings allowed in the required lint check. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib/blob/main/pyproject.toml
